purpose: A 3D Slicer scripted module ("RadVeil Defacing", Utilities) that anonymizes the face and ears of head MRI/CT volumes by calling the external `radveil` Python package, then re-runs a face detector to verify the result and shows a linked before/after 3D review. It is aimed at researchers and imaging staff who need to share de-identified head scans.
summary: Reviewed the extension source at the catalogued entry (branch `release`). The module code is clean: no telemetry, no data egress, no eval/pickle, heavy imports are lazy, the `radveil` package is installed only after a user action, and saved reports deliberately drop node/series names. Apache-2.0 with NOTICE and third-party attribution; CMake lists every shipped Python file and agrees with the catalog entry. Main caveats: the actual anonymization engine is an external PyPI wheel I could not inspect, and a user-selected segmentation node is wiped without confirmation. 🟢 Recommend merge — the three admission requirements appear met; remaining items are non-blocking.

safety.rationale: Read RadVeil.py, RadVeilLib/backend.py, conversion.py, mock_radveil.py and searched the whole tree for network/exec/pickle/subprocess: the only network use is `slicer.util.pip_install`/`pip_ensure` of the declared dependency after an explicit user click, and `urllib` only in tools/radveil_requirement.py (a developer script). No telemetry, no image upload, no eval/exec of untrusted data, no secrets; reports drop node and series names (conversion.py `_DROP_KEYS`).

environment.rationale: Nothing is installed at import or startup: backend.load() imports `radveil` lazily and installation happens only from the Install button or on first Anonymize with a confirmation (RadVeil.py installBackend/ensureBackend). The residual risk is that `radveil>=0.1,<0.2` is installed with pip into Slicer's Python and its transitive requirements are not visible in this repository, so a numpy/opencv pin inside that wheel could affect Slicer.

packaging.rationale: RadVeil/CMakeLists.txt lists RadVeil.py plus all four RadVeilLib files and the icon, and tools/stage_module.py --check (run in CI and in tests/test_packaging.py) enforces that the list matches the tree. Root CMakeLists.txt sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" and the catalog entry has build_dependencies [], build_subdirectory ".", category Utilities — consistent. The entry tracks the `release` branch, which the policy supports.

license.rationale: LICENSE is Apache-2.0 (11357 bytes, standard text) and NOTICE documents the separately installed radveil package (Apache-2.0) with its MediaPipe BlazeFace/Face Mesh (Apache-2.0) and SynthStrip (MIT) weights, plus the MRHead provenance for the README renders. Distribution permission for the extension itself is clear; the radveil package's own license files were not inspected.

soundness.rationale: Structure follows Slicer conventions (ScriptedLoadableModule/Widget/Logic/Test, parameter node, observers removed in cleanup/exit, work in a worker thread with a progress dialog, errors shown via errorDisplay, in-place overwrite confirmed). Issues found are ordinary: `_writeSegments` calls RemoveAllSegments on a user-selected segmentation, preview silently ignores the auto_threshold flag, and the landmark node is reused by name.

utility.rationale: README.md is a full user guide with install, step-by-step use, guarantees/limits, a Python/batch example and an explicit non-medical-device disclaimer; there are unit tests, an in-Slicer self-test, CI on three OSes plus Slicer Stable/Preview, screenshots and a CHANGELOG. Model provenance (MediaPipe, SynthStrip citation) and the 'review every output' warning are stated in the module help text and README.
